result.markdown:
For most startups, I'd recommend **ClickUp as the best all-around project management tool**, but the right choice depends on your startup's size, industry, and how your team operates.

The biggest mistake startups make is choosing software that's too complicated before they need it.

Here's how I'd compare the top options in 2026.

## Top 6 project management tools for startups

![Finastra Customer Story | ClickUp™](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OXxUksa73j7hoTxbYQ6zo3pspX36GflPBLMsRWXjhfWZTJdFq6md_tXaxCCc_3Kjh0xQSrUSgXoCYi3d5TOe48r-mvzFwLplQbgf4lhsH3q_bsATt_hAcyva5qI1DtZG8OasgRxxldReZAIfURcJdNdt2Br8nPVvqn-lCO5aR2MxpFl9QAiCxibf4gzehOOb?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. ClickUp**

(Best overall)

Best for all-in-one startup management

- Tasks, projects, goals, docs and dashboards.
- Highly customizable.
- Good for managing multiple departments.

**Downside\:** Can become overwhelming if overconfigured.

[Visit ClickUp](https://clickup.com/)

---

![Projects – Linear Docs](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/H7btCzSbelKXdMr_2WS3GWddG9qajBq9JZDHM8HYyOoLV6E4HDh5vlzogddffE6t5gTnGdoZ53UsXuMyPZWPmHRUwQ3ddApfS44CKAri923rLMIeylRQs9HZxmyB23G0rTfX3tmbKwJPdUtZW_x9bJsI8X8b5_Xrbg_k3vvdE22XkcL7igbp9gCGi9QLirCv?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Linear**

(Best for tech startups)

Best for product and engineering teams

- Excellent issue and bug tracking.
- Product roadmaps and sprint planning.
- Fast, clean interface.

**Downside\:** Less suited to managing an entire nontechnical business.

[Visit Linear](https://linear.app/)

---

![Project Management Hub Template by Gridvio | Notion Marketplace](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/6e1oG6Y_aW5V5yDl222hE8Y8t-T__05L0OPLqrtY2b6KrmvS_M-QH4eaVLv4afPJUAGCFGr_eoifL-Irt3_HiUqUmKW08dRjhIxW2MfVWL_nPAWNaujkMp5zdq2VbJkW7b3h6jvrTVNAFmmVU9MPLCBztqWrhslDc_LeRhpbcV451et11onvlpgBLkBnIYcR?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Notion**

(Best for early-stage teams)

Best for documentation and collaboration

- Project tracking and task databases.
- Company wiki and documentation.
- Meeting notes and planning.

**Downside\:** Less structured project execution than dedicated PM tools.

[Visit Notion](https://www.notion.com/)

---

![Introducing Dashboards - a new way to see real-time project data in charts! - Product Launches - Asana Forum](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/wCWLFp4dMEl_v-oRmbowsFC6S4_evWBQMtRxSSXp7OXP6wtqD-ndySpIhbE0vKytZ9TUoZukBYXzktu332gBeqtOvFB5r_4mn9l1GOAEawsVNLrfaNRXIZhTP4IIa9xyWd0YUcL0lL-4dUI7q2c9LjUAelrs03KqyhIOzNbo8gDFWwNUhH6KJIHf5z_4WbFK?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. Asana**

Best for cross-functional teams

- Clear task ownership.
- Project timelines and dependencies.
- Good reporting and coordination.

**Downside\:** Can get expensive as the team grows.

[Visit Asana](https://asana.com/)

---

![What's New - monday.com Product Updates](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/A6uqDbwZDZtLi6fdSQ4vBgCQbnekV0PIx4KVuVyvOr829LpE2bCzHdwMLqPfPl8gWESkzkwLYt7S32LGreo4ooKI7LMbOa3LDgEJY5XamBVn4I4fKACcjxheDQNjN3kYBWjEyVTME7rTaH0lrtDPHD2D7YT1KNXf7LC0zf16zSR-GU4N3mIXikR458xkW8a1?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. Monday.com**

Best for operations and visual management

- Visual project dashboards.
- Automations and workflows.
- Marketing, sales and operations tracking.

**Downside\:** Can be more than a small startup needs.

[Visit Monday.com](https://monday.com/)

---

![How to Toggle Trello Views: Calendar, Table, Timeline & More](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/Md351UxojPqr7NcZARTUVuAl7ocTctX4xXxse2slXCoIC1a14ed7C82Suo3_BLOf8uMvPvkR6a7txy4RworeyrfELrkzyRnZeSU5JT9wx8ysI4A-zP3PbB-iwMrUJ8znrFR0rgAWlJ-HP1EFK6mtsJMgFbfykp-Rc-ETfrBKJfKEo5IF5n0UcFY7ie8JejkV?purpose=fullsize)

**6\. Trello**

Best for simplicity and low cost

- Simple Kanban boards.
- Easy onboarding.
- Great for small teams.

## My recommendation by startup stage

| Startup stage | My pick |
|--------|--------|
| 1–3 founders | Notion |
| 3–10 employees | ClickUp |
| 10–30 employees | ClickUp or Asana |
| Tech/SaaS startup | Linear + Notion |
| 30+ employees | Asana or Monday.com |


## What I'd actually set up

For a startup, I'd organize the workspace around these six areas\:

1. **Company priorities\:** Quarterly goals and key results.
2. **Product development\:** Features, bugs and product roadmap.
3. **Marketing\:** Campaigns, content and launch plans.
4. **Sales\:** Leads, follow-ups and revenue targets.
5. **Operations\:** Hiring, finance and internal processes.
6. **Team tasks\:** Owners, deadlines and progress.

The objective is to have one place where everyone knows what needs to happen, who owns it, and when it's due.
